name: Os_EnsureDefaultValueInit_006B75B8
summary: Outlined cold path of a function-local C++ static: under compiler guard 0x007BE2D0 it zero-initialises the shared 8-byte default value at 0x007BE2D4 and releases the guard through the 0x00101A94 veneer. Same body as the rest of the Os_EnsureDefaultValueInit_* family (e.g. 0x0068A520).
evidence: Disassembly is the standard ARM EABI guard helper: push {r4,lr}; ldr r0,=0x007BE2D0; blx 0x0010009C (__cxa_guard_acquire); cmp/beq return; ldr r0,=0x007BE2D4; mov r1,#0; stm r0,{r1,r2} (8 bytes zeroed); ldr r0,=0x007BE2D0; pop {r4,lr}; b 0x00101A94 (__cxa_guard_release). Byte-for-byte the shape of the 30-member Os_EnsureDefaultValueInit_* family (0x00689770..0x0069268C), and 0x007BE2D4 is the shared default/zero pair that 81 readable functions use as the 'no value' sentinel. The old name was wrong twice: the guarded object is 0x007BE2D4, not the address the doc quoted (0x007A6874 / 0x007A6A80 / 0x007A6614 / 0x007A662C / 0x007A6620 / 0x007A6638 are literal-pool words belonging to the preceding function, never loaded by this body), and the helper is not Field-specific.

name: maybe_Gfx_GpuState_WriteScreenScale
signature: void maybe_Gfx_GpuState_WriteScreenScale(u32 arg1, u32 arg2, u32 width, u32 height)
summary: Emits the screen-scale GPU state: converts the two float arguments and the reciprocal of the requested screen size to PICA 24-bit floats and appends them as (value, command) pairs for registers 0x0041..0x0044 plus a packed 0x0068 write, then caches (arg1, arg2, width, height) in the pipeline-state record at 0x007AF058+0x20..+0x2C and sets its valid byte at +0x30.
evidence: NEW: the same command-buffer idiom and the same pipeline-state global 0x007AF058 as the named Gfx_GpuState_Invalidate (0x006BA4AC) and maybe_Gfx_GpuState_WriteMaterialColor (0x006BFE40), which also start with 'uVar = 0x000F0041' and read *0x007AF058 - so this is a Gfx_GpuState_* writer, not a command-list quad builder. The resolution table is ground truth: 0x36000000 for 1024 decodes as PICA float24 (value<<8) 2^-10 = 1/1024, 0x38111111 for 240 = 1/240, so the function derives normalised 1/width and 1/height scale factors from a screen size. The old name claimed a quad and fixed-point coordinates; there is neither. Kept maybe_ because the exact PICA register names for 0x0041..0x0044 and 0x0068 are not verifiable from this repo.

name: MoLive_Decoder_GetStreamInfo
signature: u32 MoLive_Decoder_GetStreamInfo(MoLiveDecoder* self, u32 arg2, u32* info)
summary: Looks up the MoLive stream record for the decoder's stream id (self+4) and unpacks its format fields into the caller's info array according to the record type: type 1/3 fills the full 16-bit field set (info[0]=0), type 2 fills four words (info[0]=1), type 4 fills two (info[0]=2). Returns 0 on success, 7 for an unknown record type and 0xE when the lookup fails.
evidence: NEW: the address sits inside the MoLive_Decoder_* block (0x006B9694 Create, 0x006B98C0 SkipPackets, 0x006B99C4 GetPacket, 0x006B9BC0 NextPacket, 0x006B9BF8 Update) and its record lookup 0x00669A40 is in the MoLive_Stream_* block (0x00669820 MoLive_StreamMap_Find, 0x006698AC MoLive_Stream_BindPacket, 0x006693B0 MoLive_Stream_ReadPcm). The old 'Gfx_Codec' prefix was wrong - there is no graphics code here. The type switch and the 0/7/0xE return codes are read straight from the body.

name: Gfx_GpuState_MarkDirty
summary: Marks GPU state dirty: masks the requested change bits with the already-cached set (state[2]), ORs the matching shadow-register bits into state[0] and records the handled bits in state[1] (the dirty mask). Bit 0x40 also drops the two 0x84-byte cached blocks at state+0x10C and state+0x190.
evidence: NEW: it is the exact mirror of the named Gfx_GpuState_Invalidate (0x006BA4AC) - same state object *0x007AF058, same 'flags & ~state[2]' mask, but it ORs the shadow bits into state[0] and ORs the bits into state[1], which Invalidate later clears as the dirty mask. It also sits between Gfx_GpuCmd_FillSimple (0x006BA234) and Gfx_GpuState_Invalidate (0x006BA4AC), so the Gfx_GpuState_* family is confirmed and the old 'Gfx_State_ApplyChangeFlags' wording was too vague.

The body is damaged - the branch condition shows as in_NG == in_OV because the ARM blt uses the caller's flags - so the exact bounds test and therefore the precise getter name stay unproven; maybe_ at 0.4.

name: Field_Placement_TestAreaA

Writes {ok, cell} into out, or the shared zero pair 0x007BE2D4 when the box is rejected.

The A/B pair differs only in that A also runs the per-cell overlap test 0x00642248.

signature: void Field_Placement_TestAreaB(FieldPlacementResult* out, int* base, int* offset, int* size, u32* testDesc, int manager)
summary: Variant of Field_Placement_TestAreaA without the per-cell overlap test: rejects the box if Field_HitTestActors hits anything, runs only the descriptor predicate over every cell, then Gfx_Scene_QueryRect, and writes {ok, cell} or the shared zero pair 0x007BE2D4.
evidence: NEW: the caller is now the named Field_FindPlacementCellByDelta (0x003BC98C), and the callees are the named Field_HitTestActors (0x00319908) and Gfx_Scene_QueryRect (0x0065381C). Same body as 0x006E4900 minus the 0x00642248 overlap call, so the placement-test reading is confirmed.

name: maybe_std_AllocRuntimeBlock
summary: Allocates one 0x88-byte block through Mem_Alloc and clears its first byte. The terminate-state holder (0x00100102) stores the result at its +0x1C field.
evidence: The allocator is the confident Mem_Alloc, so the allocation is certain; the 0x88 size exists only in the disassembly (movs r0,#0x88) and the C++ type behind it is not recoverable, so maybe_ at 0.4.

name: maybe_std_ThrowWideRange2
signature: void maybe_std_ThrowWideRange2(const u16* msg, u32 len)
summary: Wide-character twin of 0x00100272: builds a two-byte-stride range over the message, throws it through std_vprintf_flags1, and returns 0xFFFFFFFF when the formatted length does not fit in len.
evidence: Identical to 0x001001FC apart from the literal, completing the narrow/wide range/fixed matrix of six throw helpers; the shared body is the only evidence, so maybe_ at 0.4.

name: maybe_Fs_SetTransferPriority
summary: Enables or disables the twelve transfer channels listed in the object's +0x20..+0x50 fields using the 5-bytes-per-mode table at 0x0072D710, and when the mode reaches 4 arms the bulk transfer (0x0010E5D8) with the pair at +0x10/+0x14 or cancels it (0x0010E64C).
evidence: The only in-engine caller is the named Fs_CacheSet_Initialize (0x00103724), so a cache-set transfer setup is plausible, but nothing in the body names a priority or the channels - the wording stays a hypothesis, maybe_ at 0.42.

name: maybe_Os_GetLockDepth
summary: Asserts that bit 0 of the global lock object's +4 word is set (calling 0x0010009C otherwise) and returns the object's first word.
evidence: Its only caller 0x00104FDC uses the returned value as the runtime-flag byte, so 'read a counter out of the global lock object' is confirmed; 'depth' is still a guess about that counter's meaning, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Gfx_SetFrameReadyFlag
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SetFrameReadyFlag(GfxDisplay* self, FrameRecord* rec, u8 value)
summary: Stores the value in the frame record's +0x11 byte and, while the display state is 0x300, takes the GPU lock (0x001197FC), executes the command list and releases it (0x0011980C).
evidence: No caller; the named callee Gfx_ExecuteCommandList places it in the frame submission path, but the 'ready' meaning of +0x11 remains inferred, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Gfx_SubmitValueCommand
summary: Stores the value at +0x10 of the record and submits {value} with command header 0x0B0501C8 through Gfx_IpcCmd861.
evidence: Neither the body nor the callee carries a name or channel index, so the old 'RegisterChannelName' claim stays withdrawn; only the store plus the GPU command submission is verified and there are no callers, so maybe_ at 0.35.

name: maybe_Gfx_SetFrameTimeBudget
summary: Stores the requested frame interval (in ticks) into the global frame-timing record at 0x007F2644, recomputes the derived 1000/tick value on top of the existing base, and optionally copies the five timing words to the caller.
evidence: NEW: the record at 0x007F2644 is also read by the named Gfx_OpenGpuChannel (0x0010BB34), so the frame-timing reading is supported, but the five fields still have no named readers and 'budget' remains a description rather than a proven meaning; maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Hid_GetEventObject
signature: u32 maybe_Hid_GetEventObject(HidObject* object, u32* out, u32 defaultValue, u32 b)
summary: Stores its third argument in *out, then, if the object owns a session handle at +8, sends command 0x0C through 0x0011EC40 and lets it overwrite *out with the reply. Always returns the constant 0xC8A0A7F8, so the return value carries no information.
evidence: 0x0011EC40 (command 0x0C) has this function as its only caller, so the pair is a single command wrapper; the Hid_ owner is still only an inference from the surrounding input code, so maybe_ at 0.4.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelDescriptor
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelDescriptor(ChannelBuffer* buf, int index, unsigned short* info)
summary: Copies a mask-selected descriptor into one 0x34-byte channel record of the +0x10A4 table (bit0 one halfword at +0x56, bit1 five words at +0x5C..+0x6C, bit2 twelve halfwords at +0x5A..+0x86) and sets the dirty bit 0x1000 for channel 0 or 0x2000 for channel 1.
evidence: Largest of the channel field writers; the mask semantics are certain but the old 'FilterCoefficients' guess named the content, so the neutral copy-only name stays at maybe_ 0.4.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelPan
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelPan(ChannelBuffer* context, unsigned short pan)
summary: Writes the halfword at +0x16 of the channel block and sets dirty bit 0x4000000.
evidence: 0x00112CAC (restore) replays the saved state byte +2 through it immediately before the format write, and 0x00112D98 (SetOutputMode) copies the same field from saved state, so it is confirmed to be a per-channel state field written from saved data; 'pan' remains the best guess for a 16-bit field between rate and volume, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Os_StoreThreadLocalValue
summary: Allocator shim: passes the per-thread block (0x0011F730), the global at 0x007418D0 and the two arguments to the OS command-0x08 helper 0x0011F65C.
evidence: The callee is the command-0x08 IPC request 0x0011F65C and the only caller is Mem_CommitAllocation (0x001160AC), so 'the allocator publishes a per-thread value through an OS command' is confirmed; what the value means is not, so maybe_ at 0.42.

name: maybe_Os_DestroyThreadLocal
summary: At thread exit, fetches the thread-local object (0x0011F20C) and destroys it with 0x0011F730 followed by 0x0011F698.
evidence: No callers (it is reached from a destructor/exit hook) and the two callees are still unnamed, so 'thread local' is supported only by the TLS accessor shape, not by a named neighbour; maybe_ at 0.4.

name: Os_GetTimeSnapshot
summary: Copies the eight words produced by Os_QueryTime (0x0011F5C0) into the caller's 8-word buffer - a thin public wrapper around the OS time query.
evidence: NEW: the producer is now the named Os_QueryTime (0x0011F5C0, 'queries the current system time into eight words and normalises the packed date flags'), and the body is a pure 8-word copy of its output, so the old 'Gfx_GetEventData' name was wrong on both counts (no graphics, no event). The wrapper adds nothing but the copy.

name: maybe_Os_WaitSharedBlock
summary: Waits on the handle stored in *state with svcWaitSynchronization1 (svc 0x24), asserts on a negative result, then re-opens the SDK session with Os_EnsureIpcSessionOpen.
evidence: No callers; the two parts (svc 0x24 wait plus the named Os_EnsureIpcSessionOpen) confirm the sync/session shape, but what is being waited on is still unknown, so maybe_ at 0.35.

name: maybe_Gfx_SetTextureFill
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SetTextureFill(u32 src, u32 size, int enable, u32 color)
summary: Queues PICA200 surface commands on the GPU message queue at 0x007B0070+0x58: optionally a type-5 record carrying the source/size, then a type-1 record with the fill colour.
evidence: NEW: it sits in the Gfx_SetTexture* family (0x0011F12C SetTextureSource, 0x0011F21C SetTextureSourcePair, 0x0011F35C SetTextureRegion, 0x0011F518 SetTextureBlit) that all push records to the same 0x007B0070 queue, so the family is confirmed; 'fill' still rests on the record types and the colour word, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelMode
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelMode(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, int mode, unsigned char priority)
summary: Sets a channel's play mode (byte at +0xE) and, when the mode is 0, its priority (+0x39), then marks the channel block dirty with bit 0x20000. Uses the second channel table (selector +0x131E, pointers at +0x10B4), not the +0x1322/+0x10A4 table the field setters use.
evidence: The two parallel channel tables are now distinguished - the field setters use selector 0x1322 with pointers at +0x10A4, while this and 0x00122EF8/0x00122F74/0x00123000/0x00123070/0x001230E8 use 0x131E with +0x10B4. Caller 0x0011EE78 passes mode 0/1/2, supporting the 'play mode' reading, but it stays maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelWord34
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelWord34(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned int value)
summary: Stores a 32-bit word at +0x34 of the channel block and marks it dirty with bit 0x40000. The only caller (0x0011EE78) computes the value before the call, so it is a caller-supplied parameter rather than a fixed constant.
evidence: The offset (+0x34), the dirty bit (0x40000) and the fact that the caller supplies the value are the only facts; the old evidence called the argument a 'gain', which the 0x0011EE78 call site does not prove, so maybe_ at 0.42.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelWaveData
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelWaveData(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned int* data)
summary: Copies 0x20 bytes from the caller's descriptor into the channel's wave slot (table at +0x1234 selected by the +0x1322 double-buffer index) and sets dirty bit 4.
evidence: The source table +0x1234 is the same one 0x0011302C (SetupChannelBuffers) lays out, and the 0x20-byte copy matches the per-buffer descriptor size, so 'copy the wave/buffer descriptor into this channel' is supported by two sites rather than one; only the word 'wave' remains a label, so maybe_ at 0.48.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelWord3A
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelWord3A(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned short value)
summary: Stores a 16-bit value at +0x3A of the channel block and marks it dirty with bit 0x400000.
evidence: The offset (+0x3A), the width (16-bit) and the dirty bit (0x400000) are the facts; the single caller (0x0011EE78) passes a value it has just computed, so no field meaning can be attached and maybe_ stays at 0.42.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelLoopPoints
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelLoopPoints(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned short start, unsigned short end)
summary: Writes a byte at +0xF and a halfword at +0x3E of the channel block and marks it dirty with bit 0x800000.
evidence: The paired position write (one byte plus one halfword, one dirty bit) still reads like a loop start/end pair and the single caller (0x0011EE78) supplies both values, but the offsets are the only hard evidence, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelAdpcmParams
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelAdpcmParams(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned short arg3, unsigned short b, unsigned short c, unsigned short d, unsigned short e)
summary: Writes five consecutive fields of the channel block (+0x40, +0x42, +0x44, +0x46 and the byte at +0x45) and marks it dirty with bit 0x1000000.
evidence: Five consecutive 16-bit fields written together is the shape of a decoder parameter block, and 'ADPCM' is the best candidate for a block that also has ADPCM state fields at +0x24/+0x26; the exact offsets are the only hard evidence, so maybe_ at 0.45.
